First of all, we know very little about zombie diets. It is unclear if they require a specific caloric intake to continue to function, and how long a zombie can function from a given amount of sustenance. Zombies may very well get full after only a few bites of their victim. If this is the case, then there would be plenty of body left to be reanimated in the event of an apocalyptic zombie event.

We must also consider the type of zombie outbreak when answering this question. A supernatural zombie event may not require zombies to eat at all. Their only goal might be to kill their intended target. In this case, attacking the brain is a surefire way to achieve the zombie's mission. On the other hand, a viral zombie outbreak may only require zombies to pass the disease on to their intended targets. In this case, zombies may not necessarily focus on devouring brains, and instead focus on passing the virus to new hosts.

My personal hypothesis is that a zombie virus attacks the spinal cord and controls bodies from there, so the complete retention of the brain is not necessarily required. I would guess that the truly important part of the brain is the hindbrain where primitive and basic functions are stored. This is why complete destruction of a zombie's head is enough to render a zombie inert.
